about.title: Capitola Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Capitola is a small coastal city, but its main corridors carry heavy traffic, especially where 41st Avenue meets Capitola Road and Bay Avenue near Clares Street. Public records show 33 injury collisions and 38 injured people in the most recent reporting year, with reports clustering on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., likely tied to weekend beach traffic and commuters heading home. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days right after matter: photos of the scene, witness names, and your own account fade fast, and insurance adjusters know it. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured Capitola residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at the details of your crash, explain your options under California law, and handle communication with insurers so you're not doing it alone. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers money for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Dealing with Insurance

items.title: California's Comparative Fault Rule
items.desc: Even if you're partly at fault for a crash on Capitola Road or Bay Avenue, California's pure comparative fault law still lets you recover a share of damages. An attorney can help make sure early statements to insurers don't unfairly shift blame onto you.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering Damages
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in most car accident cases. An attorney can help document these losses accurately so they're not undervalued.

items.title: A Ticking Clock on Your Claim
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity (like a city road agency) is involved. Acting early helps preserve evidence before it disappears.

items.question: I was in a crash near 41st Avenue and Capitola Road. What should I do about the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best not to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can communicate with the insurer on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Capitola car accident?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a city or county road department, may be responsible, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it helps to get advice sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
